newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials bounce back, ignore inflation.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials bounce back, ignore inflation.

text.p: Strong corporate results lifted Zimbabwe's industrial stocks to their first rise in three weeks on Thursday but illiquidity was constraining further growth, brokers said.

The industrial index, in decline since April 24, shrugged off a sharp increase in annual inflation, to put on 48.24 points or 0.47 percent after blue chips Meikles Africa, Zimsun and Seedco published positive results in line with market expectations.

"The market was greatly encouraged by the very good results that we saw," a broker said, adding that the Meikles results indicated that multi-industrial group Delta, which owns the country's biggest beverages and brewing concerns, should also weigh in with good results.

"Activity picked up markedly across the board, featuring reasonable external selling which was pretty much absorbed by the local market indicating that liquidity versus the higher interest rates is still providing a good prop for the market," said another broker.
Gains were seen in Delta up 20 to 1,710, tobacco merchants BAT which rose 50 to 1,550, Meikles plus 100 to 2,900 and drug manufacturers CAPS) which put on 300 to 2,100 cents.
Down on the day were clothing retailers Edgars EDGR.ZI) off 15 cents to 700, multi-industrial group Apex APEX.ZI dropped 30 to 220 and bankers NMB eased off a further 50 to 3,400.

Minings were firmer for the second day running, up 6.10 points on the back of firmer deals in coal miners Wankie higher by 10 cents to 540 and Ashanti which added 1,000 to 11,000 and the index closed at 1006.21.
